K15 (buying centres) was rejected as a capital problem, but the permit and returns duty on small buyers and licensed dealers was not checked.

gaps.category: Federal and state Tax Act 2025 / Joint Tax Board small-trader duties: state IRS and LIRS PAYE and Direct Assessment for sole traders, and the Nigeria Revenue Service's new TIN/NIN harmonisation
gaps.first_search: LIRS direct assessment self-employed annual return 31 March 2026 Nigeria Tax Act personal income tax sole proprietor filing
gaps.why: The Nigeria Tax Acts took effect on 1 Jan 2026 and created the Nigeria Revenue Service. Sole traders and family firms are the largest group, but the ledger holds only a company-side small-firm TIN service (score 3) and a market-levy helper. Personal income tax self-assessment, state PAYE for employers of 1-10 staff, and the deadline of 31 March each year have not been examined as a mass duty.

gaps.category: Employer pension, NSITF and ITF registrations for micro-employers (employees 3+ for PenCom; 5+ for NSITF/ITF), including the Employee Compensation Scheme
gaps.first_search: PenCom compliance certificate employers 3 or more employees enforcement 2026 NSITF certificate of compliance small business
gaps.why: K13 rejected multi-state payroll remittance as a generic payroll tool without searching. The sharper duty is the statutory employer registration and compliance certificate (PenCom Compliance Certificate, NSITF Certificate of Compliance, ITF) that small employers must show in order to win contracts and renew licences. PenCom has run enforcement drives and 2025-2026 recoveries. A done-for-you service for micro-employers is a different buyer group from payroll software.

gaps.category: Federal import and export rules for small operators: NAFDAC product registration and import permits for small food, cosmetics and drug importers, and Nigeria Customs Service licensing of clearing agents
gaps.first_search: CRFFN licence renewal customs agents B'Odogwu 2026 Nigeria; NAFDAC import permit small importers SONCAP Form M compliance
gaps.why: Category 30 covers only EUDR and export traceability. Nobody searched small importers (Form M, PAAR, NAFDAC import permit and SONCAP certificate for low-volume traders) or the thousands of small customs agents (CRFFN licensing, annual renewals, and Customs' Advance Ruling and B'Odogwu portal rollout in 2025-2026). The duty is mandatory, recurring and falls on small firms.

gaps.category: Lagos and other states' tenancy, short-let and property small-landlord duties: land use charge, tenement rates, and the Lagos Tenancy Law / Lagos Rent registration of tenancy agreements, plus the Lagos Land Use Charge demand notices
gaps.first_search: Lagos Land Use Charge 2026 demand notice payment deadline landlords; FCT ground rent default revocation 2026
gaps.why: Hotels and estate agents were covered, but private landlords and small property owners (a huge group in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt) have a recurring annual duty: Land Use Charge, ground rent, the Lagos Tenancy Law 2011 registration, and stamp duty on tenancy. The 2025-2026 Lagos Land Use Charge reforms and the Federal Capital Territory Abuja ground rent enforcement (FCTA sealing of defaulters) create deadlines. Nothing in the ledger touches it.

gaps.category: Private security and guard-related small operators beyond K07: NSCDC registration for vigilantes and private guard companies, plus the Police (SPY) and state Neighbourhood Safety Corps, and small pharmacies/clubs registers, such as Lagos nightclub, bar and event-centre licensing and the Nigeria Police firearms and licensing of hunters
gaps.first_search: POS agents registration CBN agent banking guidelines 2025 Lagos POS operators registration deadline; Lagos liquor licence bars renewal LASAA
gaps.why: Police-facing registers are thin. K07 covers guard companies only. Small bars, lounges, event centres, gun-owning hunters and cybercafes/ POS agents face police, state liquor and CBN agent registrations. The POS/mobile-money agent segment is huge, and CBN and NIBSS/ agent-network rules (agent KYC, tiered limits, 2024-2025 PSB agent registration and the Lagos 'POS operator' registration) were not searched under any category.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: NMDPRA (federal) issued a 22 Sep 2026 directive for immediate calibration and verification of all dispensers and totalizers, with licence revocation threatened for under-dispensing; NMDPRA and FCCPC monitor jointly under an MoU. Sealing of stations in Ogun (Jul 2026) and of unlicensed LPG retailers (Akwa Ibom). Annual operating licence renewal exists, but official 2026 renewal steps were not found. Two candidates listed.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: SEC circular of 11 May 2026 (under ISA 2025 s.3(3)(m),(n); s.240) requires collateral managers, warehouse operators and exchange-linked warehouses to apply within 90 days (about 9 Aug 2026). Fetched circular states no fees and no ongoing reporting. The ₦200-500m capital figure appears only in a law-firm summary. Warehouse-receipt systems already exist (AFEX, NCX). One weak candidate.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: The Co-operative Societies Act and the state cooperative departments govern these societies; SEC says it does not regulate them (2016 notice). Two searches found no Nigerian rules on annual returns or audits, and no vendor. Listed as unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Lagos: HEFAMAA facility registration is annual (FAQ says registration ends 31 Dec; page is about 3 years old) and facilities are sealed for non-registration. MLSCN licenses labs; ISO 15189 accreditation is voluntary. NHIA Act 2022 and the Lagos 2024 executive order make health insurance compulsory, with enforcement in Lagos from Feb 2026. HMO claims desk is K03 and was not re-checked. One new candidate (licensing and accreditation pack), distinct from K03.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: PCN premises renewal deadline is reported inconsistently (31 Jan in a 2022 report; 31 Mar in PCN's March 2025 newsletter). PCN is sealing premises (Aug 2026 report: 430 of 601 premises in Yobe sealed). NDLEA precursor or controlled-drug register rules were not found. NAFDAC runs precursor import permits (2018 guidance, review date 31 May 2023). Weak candidate listed. PPMVs are K14 (rejected).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Federal Ministry of Labour Recruiter's Licence has two classes (employment agency, labour contractor). Renewal is digitised via NELEX. Applications reportedly need NSITF and ITF proof, client contracts and a health insurance document. A House committee found only 14 of 21 agencies registered with NSITF. Guard companies are K07. One weak candidate.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Mining Cadastre Office revoked 1,633 titles for unpaid annual service fees (2023). A 2025 notice of intended revocation named 1,957 initial defaulters with a 30-day window. A separate notice listed 1,263 licences to be deleted, including 144 quarry licences; the two figures are not reconciled. Ministry set a 2025 deadline for Community Development Agreements: only 342 signed against more than 2,300 titles. NCDMB launched a Nigerian Content compliance certificate portal (Aug 2026). Lagos building-control and site-register rules not searched. Two candidates listed.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: LASRERA (Lagos) licenses estate agents annually and fines unregistered practice (fine amounts unverified). SCUML covers estate surveyors/valuers and DNFIs; EFCC has pressed the real estate sector, and an older report says REDAN membership is required. No 2026 SCUML return deadline found. K08 covers only motor and jewellery dealers. One new candidate for agents. Notaries not searched.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Lagos Hotel Occupancy and Restaurant Consumption Law 2009: 5% consumption tax, operators are collection agents, monthly returns to LIRS, registration within 30 days (PwC alert, Mondaq). Lagos Hotel Licensing Law and a later tourism licensing law; the federal NTDA Act overlaps, and NIHOTOUR disrupted Lagos hotels in June 2025 (HOMAL calls it illegal). In 2014 only 350 of over 3,000 hotels and restaurants were fully registered. No guest-register rule found. Current 5% rate not re-confirmed after the 2025 tax reform. One candidate.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: EUDR applies to medium and large operators from 30 Dec 2026, with micro and small operators getting about six more months. About 300,000 Nigerian cocoa farmers; exporters bear mapping costs of USD 30-80 per tonne. TraceX and Agrolinking AgTrail are already selling to this market. NEPC exporter registration is online (e-registration) and limited to incorporated companies. No fish or timber search. Two candidates listed.

coverage.category: 31. CAC annual returns, persons with significant control and strike-off (country-specific: CAMA 2020, public notices of July 2026)
coverage.found: CAC public notice dated 15 Jul 2026: about 100,000 companies listed for strike-off, 90 days to file outstanding annual returns plus PSC data (CAMA 2020 s.692(3),(4)). Separate notice dated 7 Jul 2026: letterhead and document disclosure enforced from 1 Aug 2026 (s.304(3)). Annual returns under s.417. Sources disagree on the annual-return date (42 days after AGM vs 30 Jun for business names). Nothing found on bulk-filing software.

coverage.category: 32. Data protection compliance audit returns (country-specific: NDPA 2023 and GAID 2025)
coverage.found: Only 'major importance' controllers at Ultra-High or Extra-High level file the CAR, through licensed DPCOs; 2025-year deadline was extended from 31 Mar to 30 May 2026; late fee is 50% of the filing fee. Small businesses appear mostly outside it; the 5,000-data-subject threshold is from one source only. Weak.

coverage.category: 33. Courier and logistics licensing (country-specific: NIPOST courier regulations)
coverage.found: NIPOST licenses courier firms; reported renewal fees are ₦350,000 (domestic), ₦500,000 (indigenous international) and ₦1.5m (international), undated. NIPOST revoked 30 licences for non-renewal; 70% compliance in Enugu (Apr 2024). Fee changes have been disputed. No dispatch-rider rules found.

coverage.category: 34. Lagos State Safety Commission safety compliance certificates (country-specific, Lagos)
coverage.found: Safety Compliance Certificates (provisional 90-day, then full). Annual audit for co-working spaces and tech hubs (₦50,000 documentation fee and ₦100,000 certification fee, from 2022). A 2026 briefing reports more than 3,500 construction sites certified and 641 hospitality risk audits. A news report says about 2,800 sites and businesses were sealed over safety infractions. No official LSSC renewal page found.

coverage.category: 35. Nigeria Tax Acts 2025 small-company and TIN regime (country-specific, federal, effective 2026)
coverage.found: Small companies are exempt from CIT but must still hold a TIN, keep records and file returns; the turnover threshold is reported inconsistently (₦100m vs ₦50m). Reported filing penalties rise to ₦100,000 plus ₦50,000 per month (unverified). Tax authority is now NRS. Practitioner cockpit is K05; payroll remittances K13 (rejected).

coverage.category: 36. NHIA certificate and compulsory health insurance for employers (country-specific: NHIA Act 2022, Lagos Executive Order 2024)
coverage.found: NHIA Act 2022 defines residents to include employers with 5 or more staff. A presidential directive tells MDAs to require a valid NHIA certificate for licences, permits and procurement (date disputed between Sep 2025 and Feb 2026). Lagos requires LASHMA or NHIA-accredited cover for residents and workers, with enforcement from Feb 2026 and a policy change due 1 Aug 2026.
